cards.title: Security & Lockdown — Run, Hide, Tell
cards.body:
By the end of this session you can:
- remember the three steps in order
- choose between running and hiding
- tell the police what they need to know

cards.title: Know it before you need it
cards.body: We all hope never to use this. In the very rare event of a violent attack, such as someone with a weapon, the national advice is simple: Run, Hide, Tell. Knowing it in advance means you can act fast instead of freezing, and that can save lives, including your own.

items.title: Run
items.text: Get away if there is a safe route.

items.title: Hide
items.text: If you cannot run, get out of sight.

cards.title: Run
cards.body: RUN comes first. If there is a safe route away from the danger, take it and get yourself and others to safety.

left.title: Do
items: Encourage others to come with you

right.title: Do not
items: Waste time persuading someone who will not move

cards.title: Hide
cards.body: If you cannot safely run, HIDE. Get out of sight and stay quiet and still until help arrives.

items.title: Barrier
items.text: Put a solid barrier between you and the danger.

cards.title: Tell
cards.body: TELL is the final step. When it is safe to do so, call 999 and give the police whatever you know.

cards.title: Follow instructions exactly
cards.body: When armed police arrive, follow their instructions exactly, keep your hands visible, and do not make sudden movements. Help others stay calm, but never try to be a hero. Your safety comes first.

cards.title: Remember
cards.body:
- Run, Hide, Tell
- Run first: leave belongings behind
- If you cannot run, hide, barricade and silence your phone
- Tell: call 999 when it is safe
- Never try to be a hero

cards.q: What are the three steps to remember?
options: Stop, Think, Tell
Hide, Call, Wait
Run, Hide, Tell
Lock, Run, Wait
cards.why: The national advice is Run, Hide, Tell, in that order.

options: Grab your belongings first
Freeze in place until told otherwise
Go back for colleagues
Escape to safety, leaving belongings
cards.why: Leave your belongings behind. Nothing you own is worth going back for.

cards.q: If you cannot safely run, you should hide.
cards.why: If you cannot safely run, hide: get out of sight, barricade the door and stay away from windows.

cards.q: While hiding, your phone should be…
options: On loud so people can find you
Ringing so police can find you
Silenced completely
On vibrate only
cards.why: Silence your phone completely, not just vibrate, so it does not give you away.

cards.q: When you "Tell", who do you call and what do you tell them?
options: Your manager, and which room you are in
Call 999 and tell the police what you know
A colleague, so they can pass it on
The venue owner, and who is on shift
cards.why: Call 999 and tell the police where, what, how many attackers and what they look like.

cards.q: You should try to be a hero and tackle the attacker.
cards.why: Never try to be a hero. Your safety comes first.

cards.q: When armed police arrive you should…
options: Run towards them to explain
Follow their instructions, hands visible
Hide from them until they leave
Ask to see their identification
cards.why: Follow their instructions exactly, keep your hands visible and do not make sudden movements.

cards.q: You should leave your belongings behind when you run.
cards.why: Nothing you own is worth going back for.

cards.q: You should not waste time trying to persuade someone who will not move to come with you.
cards.why: Encourage others to come, but do not waste time persuading anyone who will not move.

cards.q: Why silence your phone completely when hiding?
options: It stops the battery running out
So the police can hear you instead
So it does not give away your location
So you can still hear a call from your manager
cards.why: A ringing or buzzing phone can give away where you are. Stay quiet and still until help arrives.
